definitions.explanation: A wild canine known for living and hunting in packs. The Japanese wolf is now extinct, but wolves remain important in Japanese folklore.

examples.japanese: {狼|おおかみ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{遠吠|とおぼ}え→遠吠え：14431_tooboe⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{聞|き}こえた→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧。
{狼|おおかみ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{群|む}れ→群れ：00298_mure⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{行動|こうどう}する→行動：02728_koudou⟧⟦{動物|どうぶつ}→動物：01480_doubutsu⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: Wolves are animals that act in packs.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧{狼|おおかみ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{明治時代|めいじじだい}→明治時代：28080_meijijidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{絶滅|ぜつめつ}した→絶滅：03756_zetsumetsu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: It is said that the Japanese wolf went extinct in the Meiji era.

notes:
{狼|おおかみ} refers to wolves.

Common expressions:
- {狼|おおかみ}⟦{少年|しょうねん}→少年：03238_shounen⟧ (the boy who cried wolf)
- ⟦{一匹|いっぴき}→一匹：08930_ippiki⟧{狼|おおかみ} (lone wolf - someone who acts alone)
- ⟦{狼狽|ろうばい}する→狼狽：08683_roubai⟧ (to be flustered - uses the kanji for wolf)
- ⟦{送|おく}り→送り：noentry⟧{狼|おおかみ} (a man who escorts a woman home with ulterior motives)

Counter: ⟦{匹|ひき}→匹：00939_hiki⟧ or ⟦{頭|とう}→頭：18067_tou⟧

Cultural note:
The ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧{狼|おおかみ} (Japanese wolf) went extinct around 1905. In Japanese folklore, wolves were revered as messengers of mountain gods (⟦{大口真神|おおくちのまかみ}→大口真神：noentry⟧) and protected crops from wild boars and deer. Several shrines still worship wolves, such as ⟦{三峯|みつみね}→三峯：noentry⟧⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧ in Saitama.
